factProposals.value: Two-way GIS sync: work order updates are written to GIS assets, and asset edits in GIS (address, coordinates, name, type, attributes) are pulled into open work orders by polling a numbered change list. Built against a stand-in GIS.

gis_log records every GIS call attempt with operation, asset, attempt number, outcome (ok, error, timeout, unauthorized), error, start and finish time; gis_cursor records how far through GIS's change list has been processed.
GIS access needs a credential, read only from the GIS_TOKEN environment variable; it is never logged or committed, and a refused credential is not retried.
factProposals.evidence: server/gis.js (gisTokenFromEnv, isRetryable); tests/gisSync.test.js (unauthorized, credential never appears)

factProposals.value: A system actor, gis-sync, appears in the audit trail for changes that came from GIS.
GIS changes to an asset are not applied to work orders that are already completed; the skip is reported.
factProposals.evidence: server/gisInbound.js (applyChange); tests/gisSync.test.js (completed work order is left untouched)

factProposals.value: Whether the city GIS offers a change list or edit tracking to poll, and how its credentials are issued, is not known; the polling interface is an assumption.

decisions.statement: Pull GIS changes by polling a numbered change list rather than receiving webhooks.
decisions.rationale: Needs nothing set up on the city's side, and a saved cursor makes it safe to run repeatedly.

decisions.statement: GIS owns asset-derived fields; the work order system owns work order fields.
decisions.rationale: The two sides never write the same field, so no conflict resolution is needed.

decisions.statement: Apply each GIS change, its audit entries and the cursor advance in one transaction, and stop at the first change that fails.
decisions.rationale: No change is applied twice or half-applied, and GIS's order of changes is kept.
decisions.evidence: server/gisInbound.js; tests/gisSync.test.js (rolled back, connection is lost)

decisions.statement: Require a logger to create a GIS client and log one row per attempt.
decisions.rationale: Makes the Trust criterion structural: no code path can call GIS without being logged.

decisions.statement: Do not retry GIS calls refused as unauthorized.
decisions.rationale: Retrying a bad credential does not help and can lock the account.

limitations.statement: processGisChanges() is not run on a schedule yet; it must be called.
The stand-in GIS keeps its change list and edits in memory only.
One failed GIS change blocks later changes until it applies, by design; a permanently failing change would need manual attention.
The demo reads the stand-in GIS directly to display asset state; those display reads are not GIS interactions of the system and are not logged.
New assets created in GIS, and assets deleted from GIS, are not handled; only edits to assets already linked to work orders are applied.
